function: Designs the ISAC transmit waveform for K users and multi-target sensing, minimizing multi-user interference plus beampattern and cross-correlation loss (pp. 3-4).
system: BS with two ULAs (16 transmit and 16 receive antennas; 64 transmit also), 4-8 single-antenna users, no RIS; carrier band not stated (pp. 2, 4-5).
method: Fully connected ANN (three hidden layers, Lambda output layer enforcing the power constraint), unsupervised training with a custom ISAC loss, Adam optimizer, PyTorch (p. 4).
data_channel: Self-generated Monte Carlo data: Rician channel (Rayleigh at K-factor 0), line-of-sight targets, QPSK symbols, 5x10^6 samples; no 3GPP or measured data (pp. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Same simulated channel for training and testing; 60% training, 20% testing, 20% online prediction samples; sweeps over SNR, trade-off weight, antennas 16/64, users 4/6/8 (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned only: analytical designs of [1] (sensing-centric omnidirectional and directional beampattern, SDR-based solution) and a genie-aided zero-interference bound; no learned baseline (p. 4).
metrics: Achievable sum rate, average rate per user, probability of detection, Cramer-Rao bound, and floating-point operation complexity (pp. 1, 4-5).
complexity: Complexity order O(K MT^2 tau_d + K MT tau_d^2) versus O((MT tau_d)^3.5) for the SDR baseline; no measured runtime or parameter count (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 2: "It is modeled via Rician distribution". The BS-user channel is a custom Rician model (Rayleigh at K-factor 0, p. 4) generated by the authors' own Monte Carlo simulation; no 3GPP TR 38.901 model, DeepMIMO ray tracing, or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 4: "We assign 60 % and 20 % of the total samples for training and testing, respectively". The test set is held out from the same simulated data; the sweeps over MT = 16/64, K = 4/6/8 and Rayleigh/Rician are separate configurations, and the paper never states that a model trained in one is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 4: "We compare our learning-based ISAC waveforms with the analytical baselines in [1]". All baselines are non-learned (analytical, SDR-based, genie-aided bound); the learned ISAC designs [6]-[8] are cited on p. 1 but never compared, so no learned baseline is present.
q4_support: p. 4: "The overall complexity of the proposed learning-based ISAC waveform design is given by" O(K MT^2 tau_d + K MT tau_d^2), compared with the O((MT tau_d)^3.5) of the SDR baseline in the same section.
q5_support: p. 4: "Our ANN is implemented via Pytorch." The training data are self-generated by Monte Carlo simulation (p. 4); no code or data link, DOI, or public channel dataset is given anywhere in the letter.
notes: Included: letter that proposes an unsupervised ANN for ISAC waveform design and reports quantitative results (pp. 4-5); the BS is MIMO, so no single-antenna exclusion. Area 5 (waveform serving sensing and communication). q3 is 0 because only analytical baselines of [1] are compared. The text prints 'f = 3.2, MHz' (p. 4) without definition, so no carrier band is recorded. Table I and Fig. 3 were read as page images (pp. 4-5). Title on p. 1: Unsupervised Learning-Based ISAC Waveforms; DOI printed on p. 1 matches.
